articles.headline: PASSED!! THE FENCE LAW ESTABLISHED AND THE HERD LAW REPEALED!!
articles.text:
The news was received last Friday that the Legislature had done a good action and earned the lasting gratitude of the stock industry by a repeal of the herd law and the establishment of a fence law.

To the energy of Mr. McCall, of Lawrence county and the active co-operation of all the other Hills members, Messrs. Wells, Washabaugh, Martin, Gregg and Sprague is due the establishment of this law. To them, more than to anyone else we looked for support of the measure, as there is a strict fence law in the Hills, and nobly did they do their work.

As first introduced by Mr. McCall, the bill called for a repeal of the herd law and the establishment of a fence law in the counties of Fall River, Custer, Pennington, Lawrence, Butte, Harding, Villard and Billings. Owing to the seeming lack of interest in his bill from Villard and Billings, Mr. McCall was on the point of striking out these two counties, when the committee from here went to Bismarck and induced him by a plain statement of facts to add the counties of Burdick, Ewing, Bowman, Dunn and McKenzie to the list already mentioned, in short, the whole western tier of counties from the Nebraska line on the south, to about sixty-five miles north of the rail-road on the north, embracing an extent of country about three hundred and twenty-five by fifty miles. In comparison to the whole of Dakota this is a very small part, but it contains the most of the valuable grazing territory.

Right here we wish to correct what we find to be a very prevalent opinion and one that was brought forward as a prominent reason why the bill should not pass. The establishment of the fence law by no means prohibits agriculture, but rather protects it, as it puts the industry exclusively into the hands of those who intend to follow it legitimately and not to see to what extent they could cinch the stockmen in blackmailing damages. To the former class, the stockmen never had any objection except to regard them with a kind of pity and to the latter class they can now bid defiance.

There was considerable opposition to this bill and it may be well to show the justice of its passage. There is but very little agriculture in the western tier of counties, the whole tier being practically given up to grazing. In a great part the whole country is unfit for agriculture, and with the exception of the Hills counties, the stock interests outnumber all others combined over a hundred to one. From the very nature of the country, this is not only so now but will be for all time. Except in a very few cases it is impossible to find a large enough tract to farm profitably and it almost invariably happens that such tracts are perfectly devoid of water. Where was the justice, then, in laying an onerous burden on stock interests and putting it in the power of the few to legally rob the many. Especially where was the justice, when there are so many other portions of Dakota for better fitted for agriculture and none others at all comparable to the Bad Lands for grazing. The Legislature has simply righted a wrong by passing the bill.

At the same time with this bill there was passed another, which we spoke of in a previous issue. It was the bill in reference to the changing of the boundary lines of Billings, Villard and Dunn counties. Before the passage of this bill, the counties ran east and west, with Dunn on the north, Billings in the middle and Villard on the south. The present boundaries of Billings county run on a north line which used to be the north line of Dunn county and if the latest maps are right, runs about ten miles south of the mouth of Beaver. The west line is the Montana line, the south line nearly cuts Chalk Buttes forty miles south of the railroad and the east line is about six miles east of Sully Springs. This bill, dividing the county, was not a popular one, and if it had been brought to a vote of the people, would have been defeated about seven to one. However, it was known that the fate of one bill depended in a measure on the other, and as the county was not organized, no direct opposition could be made. For the information of those who may wish to know, we will state here that Billings county as it was is responsible for all debts taxed up against the county and not Billings county as it is. In other words the territory making the debt is responsible for it, no matter whether its name is changed or not. Consequently the Villard county that is will have a good share of Billings county's debt to pay upon organization, a contingency not at all calculated upon by the framers of the bill.

It might be well also to state that the present eastern line of Billings county is the western line of Villard, that eastern extensions of Billings' north and south lines form the north and south lines of Villard.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy celebrates the Legislature's repeal of the herd law and establishment of a fence law for the western tier of Dakota counties, credits the Black Hills members, and explains the new Billings, Villard and Dunn county boundaries.

articles.text: Gen. Grant's condition is hourly growing worse and the opinion of the best physicians is that he connot live more than a week.
articles.summary: Note that General Grant's health is failing.

articles.text: We are in receipt of "The Wonderland" from Chas. S. Fee, describing fully the Yellowstone Park and handsomely illustrated. It will do much toward bringing tourists to the National park.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy acknowledges the Northern Pacific's Yellowstone booklet "The Wonderland" from Chas. S. Fee.

articles.text: President Cleveland is consistent in his civil service reform ideas and as a consequence, the hungry horde of Democratic office-seekers at Washington are developing a gigantic capability for kicking. Very few changes have been made in comparison to the whole number of offices and the policy seems to be to comply as strictly as possible with the rules of civil service reform.
articles.summary: Comment on President Cleveland's adherence to civil service reform.

articles.headline: STOCK NOTES. Estrayed.
articles.text: From M. S. & F. Co., October 5, one sorrel horse; four white feet, white stripe in face, branded -Y- on left shoulder and [square brand] on left thigh. A reward of $25 will be paid for information leading to his recovery.
articles.summary: Medora Stage & Forwarding Co. offers $25 reward for a sorrel horse estrayed October 5.

articles.headline: Strayed or Stolen.
articles.text: From Little Missouri, July 6, 1884, a bay horse, eight years old and weighing about 1,000 pounds. The horse was branded with an anchor on left cheek and a hat brand on left shoulder. On the left hip he had a Texas brand, looking something like 7N, connected with flourish at top of N. A reward of $25 will be paid for information leading to his recovery. The horse is the property of John Pohl, and information can be brought or sent to the Cow Boy office.
articles.summary: John Pohl offers $25 reward for a bay horse strayed or stolen from Little Missouri on July 6, 1884.

articles.text: The Wyoming Stock Growers' Association will hold its anual spring meeting April 6, at Cheyenne.
articles.summary: Wyoming Stock Growers' Association spring meeting set for April 6 at Cheyenne.

articles.text: The Little Missouri stockmen's Association meets in Medora, April 1. Time and place will probably be decided before next issue.
articles.summary: The Little Missouri stockmen's association will meet in Medora on April 1.

articles.text: A week ago Tuesday, six inches of snow fell in the Pandhandle district in Texas. The stockmen were a little fearful of the result.
articles.summary: Six inches of snow fell in the Texas Panhandle.

articles.text: The Miles City stock meeting will be held April 2nd and 3rd. Those wishing to attend from here can easily make both meetings by taking the evening train the evening of the 1st.
articles.summary: Miles City stock meeting set for April 2-3; Medora stockmen can attend both meetings.

articles.text: After diligent search only two more dead cattle have been found on the Bad Lands cattle Co's range, in addition to the nine already reported. There must certainly be others but the scarcity of carcasses indicates that the loss is hardly more than it would be from natural causes.
articles.summary: Only two more dead cattle found on the Bad Lands Cattle Co.'s range; winter loss appears light.

articles.text: There is very little danger to fear for the stock interests now, in the Bad Lands. Spring is well advanced and except for the usual shrinkage in flesh consequent upon the appearance of new grass, cattle will constantly improve in condition until the beef round-up.
articles.summary: Spring is well advanced and Bad Lands stock is out of danger.

articles.text: Messrs. Lamb & Holland of Boston, have bought Billy Paddock's ranch down the river and will immediately begin buying cattle with which to stock it. We are more than pleased to welcome these two gentleman among us as they will make first-class citizens and are certain to succeed in the cattle business.
articles.summary: Lamb & Holland of Boston have bought Billy Paddock's ranch down the river and will stock it with cattle.

articles.text: Harry Tarbell, of the Little Missouri Horse Co., is decidedly in favor of using large mares as breeders. The great call now-a-days is for large horses and although pony mares can be bought cheaper than large ones, it will take so long to breed up to the required size that money is lost in the operation.
articles.summary: Harry Tarbell of the Little Missouri Horse Co. favors large mares for breeding.

articles.text: The maverick question should come up for consideration at the next meeting of our association. We suggest that it would be an excellent plan to apply the proceeds to the school fund. Other associations have done this very satisfactorily and it will be a cheap way for the cattle men to bear their share of school expenses.
articles.summary: The Cow Boy suggests the stockmen's association apply maverick proceeds to the school fund.

articles.text: In a moment of temporary aberration we once indited a sonnet to "Chinook." We did hope to be forgiven for it but our contemporaries are ruthless in their revenge. They lighten the burden very materially, however, by crediting it to any other cattle paper in the country except the Cow Boy. The article also brings forcibly mind the old saw: "Great minds run in the same channel," for at least seven others editors wrote exactly the same article a week or two after it appeared in the Cow Boy. It may seem strange, but it must have been original with all of them, as it was not even credited to some other paper.
articles.summary: Packard complains that other papers reprint his "Chinook" sonnet without crediting the Cow Boy.

articles.text: Experiments will be made by the Co. this seasan to secure a profitable feed for the cattle that are to held here for winter markets. It would be a good plan if others would also try experiments, as it is liable to be a profitable undertaking for those who will have weak cattle to feed. There is not much doubt that alfalfa will grow well, although its cultivation has never been tried here. There are several other kinds of grasses which are claimed to be equal or superior to alfalfa. There is no telling but that a year may come when it will be impossible to put up hay and a supply of alfalfa would be a god-send.
articles.summary: "The Co." will experiment with feed such as alfalfa for cattle held over for winter markets.

articles.text: The result of several experiences has taught that it is not a good plan to keep water holes open during the winter. Animals that are supplied from these holes seem to totally lose their rustling instincts. They will fill themselves with water and stand around the hole until they are completely exhausted from cold and hunger. There is scarcely any feed on the river bottom and cattle must drift back to get grass. When forced to it cattle seem to do as well on snow as they do on water and as it is impossible to find water and feed together it is far better to keep cattle off the river in winter and compel them to develop rustling instincts. Each stockmen should in the fall make a determined effort to run cattle off the river and keep them off. It means a sure loss in condition and probable death to all cattle that stay on the river bottom, especially if they can find a water hole to stand around. Experience is the best teacher and it has certainly taught the above facts.
articles.summary: Advice against keeping water holes open in winter; cattle should be kept off the river bottom.

articles.text: The difference in opinion concerning the price of running a herd per head is remarkable. It varies from ninety cents to three dollars per year. Of course, much of this difference is due to the difference in the size of the herds, the larger ones being run proportionately, much cheaper. There is also a vast difference in the ranch expenses, with the profitable side, we believe, in favor of a liberal, rather than an economical policy. This will increase the cost of keeping, per head, but it will more than be made up by a decrease in loss. For instance, line-riding is an expensive thing to keep up and the outfits that practice it are liable to have larger expenses per head than those that do not. We will guarantee, however, that these outfits will not stop line-riding on this account for the cost is far more than made up in rescuing poor cattle and calves from death. Thus it is manifest that the outfit which spends the least money may in reality, be the most expensively conducted and vice versa. These remarks are occasioned by the fact that several exchanges quote the proportionate price for running different outfits as illustrating good or bad management.
articles.summary: Editorial on the cost per head of running a herd, defending line-riding.

articles.text: Mrs. James Harmon went east this morning.
articles.summary: Mrs. James Harmon left for the east.

articles.text: Abe Christopherson has gone to Mingusville.
articles.summary: Abe Christopherson has gone to Mingusville.

articles.text: Mrs. Lloyd Roberts came in Tuesday from the ranch.
articles.summary: Mrs. Lloyd Roberts came in from the ranch Tuesday.

articles.text: The Co. is building an additional barn south of the old one.
articles.summary: "The Co." is building an additional barn.

articles.text: Superintendent Smith, of the stage road, came in from the line Wednesday.
articles.summary: Stage superintendent Smith came in from the line Wednesday.

articles.text: The Marquis is expected back to-night and will then start for the Hills on to-morrow's coach.
articles.summary: The Marquis de Morès is expected back tonight and leaves for the Black Hills on tomorrow's coach.

articles.text: There is considerable Black Hills fright in the freight house which will soon be forwarded.
articles.summary: Black Hills freight waiting in the Medora freight house.

articles.text: The roads are in poor condition everywhere and slow time will be made for a month or two.
articles.summary: Roads are poor everywhere; slow travel expected.

articles.text: One of the bronco's brought down by Johnny Goodall, fell and hurt himself so severely that he had to be shot.
articles.summary: A bronco brought down by Johnny Goodall was injured and shot.

articles.text: John Wardenburg and his men have been engaged painting the slaughter house and other buildings lately.
articles.summary: John Wardenburg's crew painting the slaughter house.

articles.text: W. H. Stephens, formerly agent of the stage Co. in Spearfish, came up on Sunday's coach on his way to Salem, Mo.
articles.summary: W. H. Stephens, former stage agent in Spearfish, passed through on Sunday's coach.

articles.text: There was a hard snow-storm beginning at Cave Hills and extending down south of South Moreau, last Monday.
articles.summary: Hard snowstorm from Cave Hills south past the South Moreau last Monday.

articles.text: J. B. Walker is running the Pyramid Park hotel up to a high standard of excellence. We know where of we speak.
articles.summary: J. B. Walker is running the Pyramid Park hotel well.

articles.text: George Wilkes' bat is still alive and will soon be sent east for exhibition. It is well worth any one's while to see it.
articles.summary: George Wilkes' bat will be sent east for exhibition.

articles.text: Mrs. J. D. Garver and Mrs. Geo. Fitzgerald are both sick. In both cases it was due to too great exertion after recent illness.
articles.summary: Mrs. J. D. Garver and Mrs. Geo. Fitzgerald are sick.

articles.text: The constant high water and gradual melting of ice and snow takes away almost all chance of a flood of the Little Missouri.
articles.summary: Gradual melting makes a Little Missouri flood unlikely.

articles.text: E. G. Paddock's livery stable is under weigh and will soon be completed. It will be a substantial addition to our buildings.
articles.summary: E. G. Paddock's livery stable is under construction.

articles.text: Sylvane Ferris returned Saturday from an extended trip in the east. He reports a good time but that there is no country like the Bad Lands.
articles.summary: Sylvane Ferris returned Saturday from a trip east.

articles.text: A lot of other machinery and the two elevators for the slaughter-house were unloaded yesterday. The boilers are expected on every train.
articles.summary: Machinery and elevators for the slaughter-house unloaded.

articles.text: The eclipse was a good deal of a failure here. The boys had just begun to put up a job on the Chinaman about the earth coming to an end when it began to grow light again.
articles.summary: The eclipse was disappointing in Medora; a prank on "the Chinaman" fell flat.

articles.text: Lloyd Roberts is still in Minnesota buying cattle on his Glendive contract. He will first take a mixed lot of cattle, sheep, hogs, &c to Jimtown and have the cattle in Glendive by the time the grass starts.
articles.summary: Lloyd Roberts is buying cattle in Minnesota for his Glendive contract.

articles.text: There will be a "murphy" race Saturday evening. The winner will receive tickets for skates and admission for one week. Next week Saturday there will be a contest of an equally novel character.
articles.summary: A "murphy" (potato) race at the rink Saturday evening.

articles.text:
The following letter explains itself:

Mister P master i was a thinken serious of startin a paper in yure county if so be as how nun is there at present. Pleis inform me by return of male so as I can get my outfit my practical experience in noospapur wirk is limited but I think i can git ther.

Yures etc.
articles.summary: A comic misspelled letter to the postmaster from would-be newspaper starter.

articles.text: Work is progressing favorably on the Hotel de Mores. The rooms have been partitioned off to much better advantage than formerly and a substantial foundation has been built. The building will be veneered and plastered, porches built on the west and south sides and additions for kitchen and laundry built on the north side.
articles.summary: Work progresses on the Hotel de Mores.

articles.text: Our worthy post-master is an authority on all specimens, relics &c. The other day he received a quarter, with the request that some specimens be forwarded. The sender did not specify how many car-loads he wanted so our w. p. m. boxed up a huge chunk of scoria, marked: "Burning Mine," a chunk of cedar marked: "Famous cedar canon," a handfull of bullets from the butte back of the target marked: "Picked up on Custer's battle field," some iron pyrites or "sulphur" as it is called in the mines marked: "Free gold specimens," a chunk of lignite coal weighing about a hundred pounds, and a piece of petrifaction "about as big as a piece of chalk" marked: "Very rare. Warranted genuine petrifaction." And still Fisher wears a smile of childlike innocence worth a hundred dollars a yard to a confidence man.
articles.summary: Postmaster Fisher's joke shipment of Bad Lands "specimens" to a correspondent.

articles.headline: NOTICE.
articles.text:
Notice is hereby given that any contracts or bills made by any of the employes of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., will not be paid or recognized unless approved by W. F. Van Driesche, Treasurer.

Marquis de Mores, Pres't.
articles.summary: Marquis de Morès, president, notifies that stage company bills need Treasurer W. F. Van Driesche's approval.

SHOOTLETS.

The leaders jack-knifed.

The six-eyed blonde has deserted us.

The United States government and his mountain howitzer did not show up.

The editorial harp is hung on the willow as far as the prize gun is concerned.

No one as yet has a sure thing on the gun and in any event all should be promptly on hand to shoot. If all should stop shooting who do not expect to win, the Gun club would soon be a thing of the past. The next shoot will begin promptly at 1:30, Saturday afternoon.

articles.text: Joe Ferris has already entered the potato race.
articles.summary: Joe Ferris has entered the potato race.

articles.text: John Warn is still holding it down in Bozeman, waiting for court to sit.
articles.summary: John Warn is in Bozeman waiting for court.

articles.text: A pair of nickle-plated club skates will be given to the best lady skater, the contest to come off in about six weeks.
articles.summary: Ladies' skating contest planned in about six weeks.

articles.text: The Bismarck steam laundry deserves to "get there" if any firm does. Promptly on the day the amount of their bill for advertising comes without word from us. Such a manner of conducting business is rare enough to call for special commendation.
articles.summary: Praise for the Bismarck Steam Laundry's prompt payment of its advertising bill.

articles.text: Robert I. Sloan came up from the Hills Sunday on his way to New York. He is chief engineer of the New York elevated railroad and was in the Hills looking up the feasibilty of a Hay creek coal road into Deadwood. He thinks it would be a paying speculation but is far more in favor of a road from Medora to to the Hills. He thinks it would be the best paying branch of the N. P. Mr. Sloan is one of the first engineers in the country and his word carries great weight.
articles.summary: Engineer Robert I. Sloan favors a railroad from Medora to the Black Hills.

articles.text: Miss Annie Brophy came down from Mingusville to the dance Tuesday evening.
articles.summary: Miss Annie Brophy came from Mingusville for Tuesday's dance.

articles.text: The Chimney Butte ranch brand, the Maltese cross, is the latest addition to our brand columns.
articles.summary: Roosevelt's Chimney Butte ranch (Maltese cross) brand ad added to the Cow Boy's brand columns.

articles.text: Mike Sexton and Andy Corcoran came in out of the wilds Tuesday evening to celebrate with St. Patrick.
articles.summary: Mike Sexton and Andy Corcoran came in for St. Patrick's Day.

articles.text: A. Young recently found the mare that he had advertised for some time. It had fallen into a sink hole about a hundred yards from his shack and smothered.
articles.summary: A. Young found his lost mare dead in a sink hole.

articles.text: The skiventeenth of Ireland was duly celebrated last night at the rink and the light fantastic and one other toe were "shook." A most enjoyable time was had.
articles.summary: St. Patrick's dance at the rink.

articles.text: Messrs. McCall, Gregg, Martin, Wells and Sprague of the Legislature, came down from Bismarck Sunday night and the three latter left in company with seven others for the Hills Monday morning. Messrs. McCall, Gregg and Geo. Bell of Spearfish, stayed over and went yesterday morning.
articles.summary: Black Hills legislators passed through Medora on their way home from Bismarck.

articles.text: Little Tommy, our Tommy, Tommy Kerr "bobbed up serenely from below," Tuesday evening. He leaves to-night for the west and again will the mantle of gloom descend upon us even as the peregrinating hen descends upon the June bug. Ke-good bye, Tommy, pe-come again.
articles.summary: Tommy Kerr visited Tuesday and leaves tonight for the west.

articles.text: The slaughter-house will be ready for business several weeks before cattle can be supplied. Work will begin as soon as there is a certainty of five hundred head a week, the capacity of the house being nine hundred head. Work will go on night and day and it is hoped that steam will not be completely shut off until next spring.
articles.summary: Slaughter-house will open once 500 head a week are assured; capacity 900.

articles.text: We are in receipt of a letter from Vic Smith, dated at Prplar Creek, March 10. He states that loss among the Wolf Point agency cattle is very heavy and that the Indians are living high on "frozen-to-death" beef. He also writes that times are booming in Medora in comparison to any other place he has found. He says nothing about his trip but we suppose he has started by this time. He gladdened the editorial heart by sending in some new subscriptions.
articles.summary: Letter from Vic Smith at Poplar Creek reports heavy cattle losses at Wolf Point agency.

articles.text: At first sight it seems like a gigantic and profitless undertaking, but the Co. will soon begin the erection of a barn capable of holding 10,000 cattle. They will be fed on hay enough to keep them in prime condition and slaughtered as they are needed. This can scarcely be called an experiment as it turned out a complete success in Duluth, where feed is much higher than it is here. The complete output for this year of the Continental cattle Co. has already been contracted. Last year it was 12,000 head. These cattle will all be killed here.
articles.summary: "The Co." will build a barn for 10,000 cattle to feed stock for slaughter; Continental Cattle Co. output contracted.

events.date_basis: "last Friday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885 (news received)
events.title: News reaches Medora that the Legislature passed the fence law
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that news arrived that the territorial Legislature had repealed the herd law and established a fence law for the western counties, including Billings, after a committee from Medora went to Bismarck to lobby Mr. McCall.
events.excerpt: The news was received last Friday that the Legislature had done a good action and earned the lasting gratitude of the stock industry by a repeal of the herd law and the establishment of a fence law.

events.date_basis: Reported with the fence-law news; passage date not given, reported "last Friday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Legislature redraws Billings, Villard and Dunn county lines
events.summary: The Cow Boy described a bill passed with the fence law that changed the boundaries of Billings, Villard and Dunn counties, said it would have been defeated about seven to one by local voters, and noted that the old Billings county's debt would fall partly on Villard county.
events.excerpt: This bill, dividing the county, was not a popular one, and if it had been brought to a vote of the people, would have been defeated about seven to one.

events.date_basis: "October 5" in an estray notice in the 19 Mar 1885 issue; year inferred as 1884
events.title: Stage company horse strays from Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy carried a notice that a sorrel horse branded -Y- had strayed from the M. S. & F. Co. on October 5, with a $25 reward offered.
events.excerpt: From M. S. & F. Co., October 5, one sorrel horse; four white feet, white stripe in face, branded -Y- on left shoulder

events.date_basis: "July 6, 1884" stated in notice
events.title: John Pohl's bay horse strayed or stolen at Little Missouri
events.summary: The Cow Boy carried a notice offering $25 for information on John Pohl's bay horse, strayed or stolen from Little Missouri on July 6, 1884.
events.excerpt: From Little Missouri, July 6, 1884, a bay horse, eight years old and weighing about 1,000 pounds.

events.date_basis: "April 1" in 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Little Missouri stockmen's association to meet in Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy announced that the Little Missouri stockmen's association would meet in Medora on April 1, with time and place to be fixed.
events.excerpt: The Little Missouri stockmen's Association meets in Medora, April 1.

events.date_basis: "April 2nd and 3rd" in 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Miles City stock meeting; Medora men can take the evening train
events.summary: The Cow Boy noted the Miles City stock meeting on April 2 and 3 and said stockmen could attend both it and the Medora meeting by taking the evening train on April 1.
events.excerpt: Those wishing to attend from here can easily make both meetings by taking the evening train the evening of the 1st.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Bad Lands Cattle Co. finds few dead cattle
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that a search found only two more dead cattle on the Bad Lands Cattle Co.'s range, eleven in all, suggesting winter losses close to natural levels.
events.excerpt: After diligent search only two more dead cattle have been found on the Bad Lands cattle Co's range, in addition to the nine already reported.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Spring well advanced on the Bad Lands range
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that spring was well advanced in the Bad Lands and cattle should improve steadily until the beef round-up.
events.excerpt: There is very little danger to fear for the stock interests now, in the Bad Lands. Spring is well advanced

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Boston men Lamb & Holland buy Billy Paddock's ranch
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Lamb & Holland of Boston had bought Billy Paddock's ranch down the Little Missouri and would begin buying cattle to stock it.
events.excerpt: Messrs. Lamb & Holland of Boston, have bought Billy Paddock's ranch down the river and will immediately begin buying cattle with which to stock it.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Packard protests uncredited reprints of his "Chinook" sonnet
events.summary: The Cow Boy complained that its sonnet to "Chinook" was being reprinted by other papers and credited to anyone but the Cow Boy.
events.excerpt: They lighten the burden very materially, however, by crediting it to any other cattle paper in the country except the Cow Boy.

events.date_basis: "this season" in 19 Mar 1885 issue; "the Co." not named
events.title: "The Co." plans feed experiments, including alfalfa
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that "the Co." would experiment this season to find a profitable feed for cattle held at Medora for winter markets, suggesting alfalfa.
events.excerpt: Experiments will be made by the Co. this seasan to secure a profitable feed for the cattle that are to held here for winter markets.

events.date_basis: "this morning" in Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Mrs. James Harmon goes east
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mrs. James Harmon went east on the morning of publication.
events.excerpt: Mrs. James Harmon went east this morning.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Abe Christopherson goes to Mingusville
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Abe Christopherson had gone to Mingusville.
events.excerpt: Abe Christopherson has gone to Mingusville.

events.date_basis: "Tuesday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Mrs. Lloyd Roberts comes in from the ranch
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mrs. Lloyd Roberts came into Medora from the ranch on Tuesday.
events.excerpt: Mrs. Lloyd Roberts came in Tuesday from the ranch.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: "The Co." builds an additional barn
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that "the Co." was building an additional barn south of the old one.
events.excerpt: The Co. is building an additional barn south of the old one.

events.date_basis: "Wednesday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Stage superintendent Smith comes in from the line
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Superintendent Smith of the stage road came into Medora from the line on Wednesday.
events.excerpt: Superintendent Smith, of the stage road, came in from the line Wednesday.

events.date_basis: "to-night" = Thu 19 Mar 1885 (issue date); coach "to-morrow" = Fri 20 Mar
events.title: Marquis de Morès expected back, then off to the Black Hills
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that the Marquis de Morès was expected back in Medora that night and would leave for the Black Hills on the next day's coach.
events.excerpt: The Marquis is expected back to-night and will then start for the Hills on to-morrow's coach.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Black Hills freight piles up at Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported considerable Black Hills freight in the Medora freight house awaiting forwarding.
events.excerpt: There is considerable Black Hills fright in the freight house which will soon be forwarded.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Roads in poor condition
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that roads were in poor condition everywhere and travel would be slow for a month or two.
events.excerpt: The roads are in poor condition everywhere and slow time will be made for a month or two.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Johnny Goodall's bronco injured and shot
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that one of the broncos brought down by Johnny Goodall fell and was hurt so badly it had to be shot.
events.excerpt: One of the bronco's brought down by Johnny Goodall, fell and hurt himself so severely that he had to be shot.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Wardenburg crew paints the slaughter house
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that John Wardenburg and his men had been painting the slaughter house and other buildings.
events.excerpt: John Wardenburg and his men have been engaged painting the slaughter house and other buildings lately.

events.date_basis: "Sunday's coach" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Former stage agent W. H. Stephens passes through
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that W. H. Stephens, formerly the stage company's agent at Spearfish, came up on Sunday's coach on his way to Salem, Mo.
events.excerpt: W. H. Stephens, formerly agent of the stage Co. in Spearfish, came up on Sunday's coach on his way to Salem, Mo.

events.date_basis: "last Monday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Hard snowstorm from Cave Hills to South Moreau
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported a hard snowstorm on Monday from the Cave Hills south beyond the South Moreau.
events.excerpt: There was a hard snow-storm beginning at Cave Hills and extending down south of South Moreau, last Monday.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: J. B. Walker praised for Pyramid Park hotel
events.summary: The Cow Boy praised J. B. Walker's management of the Pyramid Park hotel.
events.excerpt: J. B. Walker is running the Pyramid Park hotel up to a high standard of excellence.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: George Wilkes' bat to go east for exhibition
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that George Wilkes' bat was still alive and would soon be sent east for exhibition.
events.excerpt: George Wilkes' bat is still alive and will soon be sent east for exhibition.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Mrs. Garver and Mrs. Fitzgerald ill
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mrs. J. D. Garver and Mrs. Geo. Fitzgerald were both sick after overexertion following recent illness.
events.excerpt: Mrs. J. D. Garver and Mrs. Geo. Fitzgerald are both sick.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Little Missouri flood danger receding
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that constant high water and gradual melting had removed almost all chance of a Little Missouri flood.
events.excerpt: The constant high water and gradual melting of ice and snow takes away almost all chance of a flood of the Little Missouri.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: E. G. Paddock building a livery stable
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that E. G. Paddock's livery stable was under way in Medora and would soon be completed.
events.excerpt: E. G. Paddock's livery stable is under weigh and will soon be completed.

events.date_basis: "Saturday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Sylvane Ferris returns from the east
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Sylvane Ferris, Roosevelt's ranch partner, returned Saturday from an extended trip east, saying there was no country like the Bad Lands.
events.excerpt: Sylvane Ferris returned Saturday from an extended trip in the east. He reports a good time but that there is no country like the Bad Lands.

events.date_basis: "yesterday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Slaughter-house elevators and machinery arrive
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that machinery and two elevators for the Medora slaughter-house were unloaded, with the boilers expected on any train.
events.excerpt: A lot of other machinery and the two elevators for the slaughter-house were unloaded yesterday.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Solar eclipse disappoints at Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that the eclipse was largely a failure at Medora, cutting short a prank some men were playing on a Chinese resident.
events.excerpt: The eclipse was a good deal of a failure here.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Lloyd Roberts buying cattle in Minnesota
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Lloyd Roberts was in Minnesota buying cattle for a Glendive contract, to move stock via Jamestown to Glendive by grass time.
events.excerpt: Lloyd Roberts is still in Minnesota buying cattle on his Glendive contract.

events.date_basis: "Saturday evening" after Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: "Murphy" race planned at the skating rink
events.summary: The Cow Boy announced a "murphy" (potato) race for Saturday evening, the prize being a week of skate tickets and admission, with another novel contest the following Saturday.
events.excerpt: There will be a "murphy" race Saturday evening.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Hotel de Mores remodeled
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that work on the Hotel de Mores was progressing: rooms repartitioned, a new foundation, veneer and plaster, porches, and kitchen and laundry additions planned.
events.excerpt: Work is progressing favorably on the Hotel de Mores.

events.date_basis: "The other day"; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Postmaster Fisher ships joke "specimens"
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that the postmaster, Fisher, answered a request for specimens by boxing up scoria, cedar, bullets labeled as from Custer's battlefield, pyrites labeled gold, lignite and a petrifaction.
events.excerpt: a handfull of bullets from the butte back of the target marked: "Picked up on Custer's battle field,"

events.date_basis: Notice running in Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Morès requires treasurer's approval for stage company bills
events.summary: The Cow Boy carried a notice from the Marquis de Morès, president of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., that employees' contracts and bills would not be paid unless approved by Treasurer W. F. Van Driesche.
events.excerpt: any contracts or bills made by any of the employes of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., will not be paid or recognized unless approved by W. F. Van Driesche, Treasurer.

events.date_basis: Most recent (third) shoot, undated; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Bad Lands Gun Club holds third shoot
events.summary: The Cow Boy published scores of the Bad Lands Gun Club's latest shoot, a below-standard day won by Wyland, who also led the three-shoot totals; editor Packard stood fourth overall.
events.excerpt: The last shoot did not come up to the standard of the preceding shoots, owing to the weather or some other of the unaccountable reasons

events.date_basis: "Saturday afternoon" after Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Next Gun Club shoot set for Saturday
events.summary: The Cow Boy announced that the next Bad Lands Gun Club shoot would begin at 1:30 Saturday afternoon.
events.excerpt: The next shoot will begin promptly at 1:30, Saturday afternoon.

events.date_basis: Potato ("murphy") race announced for "Saturday evening" after Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Joe Ferris enters the potato race
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Joe Ferris had already entered the rink's potato race.
events.excerpt: Joe Ferris has already entered the potato race.

events.date_basis: Undated item; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: John Warn waits for court in Bozeman
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that John Warn was still in Bozeman waiting for court to sit.
events.excerpt: John Warn is still holding it down in Bozeman, waiting for court to sit.

events.date_basis: "in about six weeks" from Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Ladies' skating contest planned
events.summary: The Cow Boy announced that a pair of nickel-plated club skates would go to the best lady skater in a contest about six weeks off.
events.excerpt: A pair of nickle-plated club skates will be given to the best lady skater

events.date_basis: "Sunday" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Engineer Robert I. Sloan passes through, favors Medora–Hills railroad
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Robert I. Sloan, chief engineer of the New York elevated railroad, came up from the Black Hills on Sunday and favored a branch road from Medora to the Hills over a Hay creek coal road to Deadwood.
events.excerpt: He thinks it would be a paying speculation but is far more in favor of a road from Medora to to the Hills.

events.date_basis: "Tuesday evening" before Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Annie Brophy comes from Mingusville for the dance
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Miss Annie Brophy came down from Mingusville for the dance Tuesday evening.
events.excerpt: Miss Annie Brophy came down from Mingusville to the dance Tuesday evening.

events.date_basis: Brand ad first noted as "latest addition" in Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: Roosevelt's Maltese Cross brand joins the Cow Boy's brand columns
events.summary: The Cow Boy noted that the Chimney Butte ranch brand, the Maltese cross, was newly added to its brand columns; the ad names Theodore Roosevelt as proprietor and Ferris & Merrifield as managers, range six miles south of the N.P.R.R. on the Little Missouri.
events.excerpt: The Chimney Butte ranch brand, the Maltese cross, is the latest addition to our brand columns.

events.date_basis: "Tuesday evening" before Thu 19 Mar 1885 (St. Patrick's Day)
events.title: Sexton and Corcoran come in for St. Patrick's Day
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Mike Sexton and Andy Corcoran came in out of the wilds Tuesday evening to celebrate St. Patrick's Day.
events.excerpt: Mike Sexton and Andy Corcoran came in out of the wilds Tuesday evening to celebrate with St. Patrick.

events.date_basis: "recently"; week before Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: A. Young finds lost mare dead in sink hole
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that A. Young found the mare he had advertised for, smothered in a sink hole about a hundred yards from his shack.
events.excerpt: It had fallen into a sink hole about a hundred yards from his shack and smothered.

events.date_basis: "last night" before Thu 19 Mar 1885 (item may have been set earlier; St. Patrick's Day was Tue 17 Mar)
events.title: St. Patrick's celebration and dance at the rink
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that the seventeenth of Ireland was celebrated with dancing at the skating rink.
events.excerpt: The skiventeenth of Ireland was duly celebrated last night at the rink

events.date_basis: "Sunday night" before Thu 19 Mar 1885; departures Monday 16 and "yesterday" 18 Mar
events.title: Black Hills legislators pass through Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that legislators McCall, Gregg, Martin, Wells and Sprague arrived from Bismarck Sunday night; Martin, Wells and Sprague left for the Hills Monday, and McCall, Gregg and Geo. Bell of Spearfish left Wednesday morning.
events.excerpt: Messrs. McCall, Gregg, Martin, Wells and Sprague of the Legislature, came down from Bismarck Sunday night

events.date_basis: "Tuesday evening" before Thu 19 Mar 1885; leaves "to-night" 19 Mar
events.title: Tommy Kerr visits Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that Tommy Kerr arrived from the east Tuesday evening and would leave for the west on the night of publication.
events.excerpt: Little Tommy, our Tommy, Tommy Kerr "bobbed up serenely from below," Tuesday evening.

events.date_basis: "several weeks" ahead, from Thu 19 Mar 1885
events.title: Slaughter-house nearly ready, awaiting cattle supply
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that the Medora slaughter-house would be ready several weeks before cattle could be supplied, with a capacity of nine hundred head and plans to run night and day.
events.excerpt: Work will begin as soon as there is a certainty of five hundred head a week, the capacity of the house being nine hundred head.

events.date_basis: Letter "dated at Prplar Creek, March 10"
events.title: Vic Smith writes from Poplar Creek of heavy agency cattle losses
events.summary: The Cow Boy received a letter from Vic Smith dated March 10 at Poplar Creek saying cattle losses at the Wolf Point agency were heavy and the Indians were eating frozen beef, and that Medora was booming by comparison.
events.excerpt: He states that loss among the Wolf Point agency cattle is very heavy and that the Indians are living high on "frozen-to-death" beef.

events.date_basis: "will soon begin" in Thu 19 Mar 1885 issue
events.title: "The Co." plans a 10,000-head feeding barn; Continental Cattle Co. output to be killed at Medora
events.summary: The Cow Boy reported that "the Co." would soon build a barn to hold 10,000 cattle for feeding and slaughter as needed, and that the Continental Cattle Co.'s whole output for the year had been contracted to be killed at Medora.
events.excerpt: the Co. will soon begin the erection of a barn capable of holding 10,000 cattle.
